title: It’s hard to feel sorry for AI companies when China is giving them a taste of their own medicine
excerpt: It's time to read AI its rights
content_html:
It's no secret that AI technology is advancing faster than it can be regulated, with some execs now even saying so themselves. But it seems anything which threatens the advancement of AI must be avoided, in fear of that always present and ever dangerous ‘other’.

The latest installment of ‘please, dear God, slow down before it gets too dangerous’ comes in the form of Pacing the Frontier. Thousands of staff from frontier AI companies once again pleading for a halt in the development of AI technology.

It's all too predictable that the reason from the top for continuing development will be that China ‘threatens’ to catch up. China deploying advanced AI in the military, or in the police, or using it for spying are the threats most often cited, as if these same things aren’t happening at home and around the rest of the world.

So now that China is distilling US AI models to produce rivals at a cheaper cost, I play my tiny violin - the hypocrisy of intellectual property rights suddenly becoming important to AI companies because they could lose money is comical.

Respect my rights

The rights AI companies are citing are the same rights AI companies may have inadvertently violated in hoovering up public data to train their models in the first place, but that's still up for debate.

But AI companies can claim that this trove of public data is a trade secret as a way to prevent human creators from accessing AI training data to see (and possibly prove) that their content has been stolen. Rights for me but not for thee.

What I find funny is that the average American has more in common with the average Chinese person than they do with an AI company. Does an AI company enjoy cooking? Drawing or reading? Can it go out after work for a hot drink or a cold beer? Does it worry that if it doesn’t make any money this month everything might come crashing down? Possibly the last one.

Somehow the bond of national identity tied between a person and a corporate entity is expected to be more powerful than shared human experience. It’s also the bond that AI companies and those in power use to press the accelerator on the machine, just so long as we, the ‘good guys’, are ‘winning’.

Beware the ‘bad guys’

This myth of the external ‘other’, or the ‘bad guys’, is a powerful propaganda tool. But it only works in a vacuum. If you can directly engage with those you are told are your enemy and you find they are not so different from yourself, the myth of the ‘other’ evaporates. (Social media and the internet is a double edged sword in this regard, but that's a discussion for another time).

So if Chinese companies can produce a rival product that doesn’t annihilate a monthly token budget in a matter of days, I say let them. If you are worried about China having your data, are you not worried about who is currently collecting it? If you are worried about China deploying AI systems in the military, police, surveillance, and cybersecurity, are you not worried about it happening closer to home?

The warning that using Chinese AI models is dangerous because they can steal your business secrets is especially weak, especially when you consider Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella’s warning that US AI companies are already doing exactly that, and selling it to your competition.

So the next time an AI company complains about their intellectual property being stolen, remember that it is just the great, ever-turning wheel of innovation. Or if you are warned about the data collection policies of a foreign AI model, check the policies of the tech closer to home. You’d be surprised at just how much they already know about you.

content_html_zh:
人工智能技术的发展速度快于监管速度，这已不是什么秘密，一些高管现在甚至自己也这么说。 但似乎任何威胁人工智能进步的事情都必须避免，因为担心始终存在且永远危险的“他者”。

“请亲爱的上帝，在事情变得太危险之前，请放慢脚步”的最新一期是以“在边境上行走”的形式出现的。 数千名前沿人工智能公司员工再次呼吁停止人工智能技术的发展。

可以预见的是，自上而下继续发展的原因将是中国“威胁”要迎头赶上。 中国在军队或警察中部署先进的人工智能，或将其用于间谍活动是最常被提及的威胁，就好像这些同样的事情在国内和世界其他地方没有发生一样。

因此，现在中国正在提炼美国的人工智能模型，以更便宜的成本生产竞争对手，我拉起了我的小小提琴——知识产权的虚伪突然对人工智能公司变得重要，因为它们可能会赔钱，这很滑稽。

尊重我的权利

人工智能公司引用的权利与人工智能公司在收集公共数据来训练其模型时可能无意中侵犯的权利相同，但这仍然有争议。

但人工智能公司可以声称这些公共数据是商业秘密，以防止人类创造者访问人工智能训练数据以查看（并可能证明）其内容已被盗。 权利属于我，但不属于你。

我觉得有趣的是，普通美国人与普通中国人的共同点比他们与人工智能公司的共同点还要多。 人工智能公司喜欢做饭吗？ 画画还是读书？ 下班后可以出去喝杯热饮还是冰镇啤酒吗？ 它是否担心如果这个月赚不到钱，一切都会崩溃？ 可能是最后一张。

不知何故，个人与企业实体之间的国家认同纽带预计将比共同的人类经验更强大。 这也是人工智能公司和当权者用来踩下机器加速器的纽带，只要我们这些“好人”就能“获胜”。

谨防“坏人”

这种外部“他者”或“坏人”的神话是一种强大的宣传工具。 但它只能在真空中起作用。 如果你能直接与那些你被告知是你的敌人的人接触，并且你发现他们与你自己没有太大不同，那么“他人”的神话就会消失。 （在这方面，社交媒体和互联网是一把双刃剑，但这是另一次讨论了）。

因此，如果中国公司能够生产出一款不会在几天内耗尽每月代币预算的竞争对手产品，我会说就让他们吧。 如果您担心中国拥有您的数据，您是否不担心目前谁在收集这些数据？ 如果你担心中国在军队、警察、监控和网络安全领域部署人工智能系统，你不担心它发生在离你更近的地方吗？

关于使用中国人工智能模型是危险的，因为它们可以窃取你的商业机密的警告尤其微弱，尤其是当你考虑到微软首席执行官萨蒂亚纳德拉警告美国人工智能公司已经在这样做，并将其出售给你的竞争对手时。

因此，下次当人工智能公司抱怨他们的知识产权被盗时，请记住，这只是伟大的、不断转动的创新之轮。 或者，如果您被警告有关外国人工智能模型的数据收集政策，请检查离您较近的技术的政策。 你会惊讶于他们对你的了解之多。

Benedict 对国家支持的威胁行为者、APT 组织以及关键国家基础设施的保护进行了详细分析，他的报告弥合了技术威胁情报和 B2B 安全策略之间的差距。

Benedict 拥有白金汉大学安全与情报研究中心 (BUCSIS) 的安全、情报和外交硕士学位（优异），他的专业为他提供了一个强大的学术框架来解构复杂的国际冲突和情报行动，并能够将复杂的安全数据转化为可行的见解。
